title: Carbon dioxide in the air, over 800,000 years
reconstructed_label: Air bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice
source: Bereiter and others (2015), Antarctic ice-core CO2 composite, NOAA World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
note: In the 800,000 years before 1800, CO2 stayed between about 170 and 300 ppm. The live Mauna Loa figure is far above that range.

title: Global temperature, over 2,000 years
measured_label: Thermometer record used by the study (Cowtan and Way), to 2017
reconstructed_label: Tree rings, corals, ice and lake sediments: 31-year average, with the 95% range
source: PAGES 2k Consortium (2019), global mean temperature reconstructions, NOAA World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
note: Both lines come from the same study and use its 1961-1990 baseline. The dashboard's temperature card uses NASA's 1951-1980 baseline, so its figures are not directly comparable with these.

title: People on Earth, over 12,000 years
reconstructed_label: Historical estimates: HYDE before 1800, Gapminder 1800 to 1949
source: Our World in Data, long-run population (HYDE 2023, Gapminder 2022, UN World Population Prospects 2024)
note: Estimates before 1800 are spaced 100 to 1,000 years apart, so short-lived falls such as plagues do not show. Our World in Data notes breaks where the sources join.
